title: Developer adoption microcopy anchors and quickstart hooks
content:
TL;DR:
A bite-sized messaging brief and microcopy kit to drive developer trial-to-first-call conversion for the Hosted API. Focus: developer-first value props (fast time-to-first-infer, predictable unit costs, transparent perf), one-minute quickstart scripts, and simple pricing language that reduces churn at the payment prompt.

Audience:
- Individual engineers evaluating APIs for prototypes
- Product teams assessing integration effort and cost predictability
- Platform/infra leads who care about latency/SLOs and observability

Primary positioning anchors (developer-first wording):
1) Plug in and ship: "Get a working inference call in under 60 seconds — SDKs, samples, and a live model catalog so your first token is generated before you reach for coffee."
2) Predictable microeconomics: "Per-token pricing, live estimator, and lightweight caching guidance so your dev budget doesn't surprise you in production."
3) Production-ready from prototype: "Same API shape from free trial to dedicated capacity — rollouts, tracing, and SLAs when you need them."

Three quickstart angles (copy + flow)
A: "Zero-friction try" (target: single dev, 5–15 mins)
- Microcopy: "Create account → Get free credits → Paste sample snippet → See streaming output."
- Script: 1) Sign up (email/GitHub) 2) Open Starter Project in repo 3) Replace placeholder key 4) Run `npm start` to see streaming tokens 5) Click “Make it yours” to copy SDK snippet for your app
- Measurement: time-to-first-successful-response (goal < 60s), % who run samples

B: "From prototype to preview" (target: PM/engineer pair, 30–90 mins)
- Microcopy: "Generate completions, save to your preview page, toggle model size to test latency vs cost."
- Script: 1) Use dashboard to spin a sandbox route 2) Try two model variants (fast/accurate) 3) Enable prefix cache in SDK 4) Create simple A/B using rollout controls
- Measurement: # of routes created, toggle usage, model-change events

C: "Team signoff to committed usage" (target: platform lead)
- Microcopy: "Commit to reserved capacity or keep pay-as-you-go — both use the same API and SDKs."
- Script: 1) Export cost estimate for 100k tokens/day 2) Compare PAYG vs 1-month reserved capacity 3) Schedule a demo for SLA conversation
- Measurement: conversion to paid plan, reserved capacity interest rate

Pricing language suggestions (developer-friendly):
- Lead line: "Pay for what you use — per-token for hosted inference, per-embedding for similarity, and simple monthly commitments for predictable throughput."
- Emphasize transparency: "Live cost estimator in the console + per-route token breakdowns in logs."
- Example phrasing for the pricing page: "Small experiments: free tier credits included. Production: $X / 1M tokens for gen-v1 (fast) — switch to gen-hq for accuracy at $Y / 1M tokens. Dedicated options start at $Z/month with committed throughput."
- Micro copy for billing prompt: "Enable billing to keep your keys active. We’ll notify at 50% of free credits and again before exceeding your estimate."
- Objection handling copy:
  - "I don’t want surprise bills" -> "Set hard quotas per key and daily caps — we block overage by default unless you opt-in."
  - "I need predictable latency" -> "Pin a model variant and use Dedicated for SLO-backed latency guarantees."

Competitive quick notes (talking points for SDR/demo):
- Strengths to call out quickly:
  - Developer ergonomics: single SDK across hosted/dedicated/private, streaming + structured outputs, code samples for common frameworks
  - Observability: token-level cost breakdown + per-route latency histograms
  - Cost controls: automatic prefix caching suggestions and batching heuristics in-platform
- Competitor-friendly lines:
  - Versus large closed LLM APIs: "Open model catalog + verified performance profiles — not just one black-box pricing tier."
  - Versus self-hosted runtimes: "We give the same runtime guarantees and autoscaling, plus no infra ops for your team to run."
  - Versus other hosted vendors: "We show you both latency and token-cost tradeoffs live, and give simple knobs to move the needle."

Microcopy library (versioned):
- CTA variants for try button: ["Try the API — 5 min start", "Instant demo — run a call", "Start with free credits"]
- Onboarding step copy snippets: ["Paste your key here", "View sample repo", "Run the sample app" ]
- Error/limits copy: ["Quota reached — request extension or enable billing", "Requesting larger model: estimated cost displayed", "Latency spike — falling back to cheaper model variant."]

Sample 30s elevator script for sales ops/AE:
"Redwood lets you make your first inference call in under a minute with transparent per-token pricing and built-in cost controls. Teams run the same API from prototype to production — when you need SLOs, switch to Dedicated without changing code. It's faster to integrate and cheaper to scale."

Measure-of-success (MOS) metrics we should instrument in the next sprint:
- Time-to-first-successful-response (from sign up)
- % of new accounts that run sample app within 24h
- Billing opt-ins within first 7 days (free credits exhausted or billing enabled)
- Number of routes created, model toggles per account

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we show explicit example unit prices in the trial onboarding flow or keep a link to the pricing page? (tradeoff: friction vs clarity)
- Finalize the default microcopy tone: pragmatic-technical vs friendly-helpful? (ops: Liam to A/B test 2 variants on signup modal)
- How aggressively do we surface Dedicated / Reserved options inside the free console? (risk: premature up-sell)

Next steps (owners and short timeline):
- Draft A/B copy for signup modal (Priya + Liam) — 1 week
- Implement 30s sample repo and update README microcopy (Sofia) — 2 weeks
- Wire up console estimator to show token-cost for sample project (ENG-UI ticket linked: JIRA-7890) — 3 sprints
- Prep sales one-pager with pricing comparatives and competitive lines (GTM lead) — 2 weeks

Notes/to-self and references: 
- Reference: internal perf profiles (CON-3421) for fast vs accurate model costs
- Slack thread: #product-hosted-api / thread on rollout prompts (see pinned messages)

Rough copy snippets to lift into UI (editable):
- Signup header: "Start building with Redwood — free credits included"
- Sample success state: "Nice! Your app made its first call. Want to embed this sample into your preview?"
- Billing CTA inside console: "Enable billing to unlock larger quotas and reserved capacity pricing"

Appendix: short competitor messaging cheat-sheet (for AE brief):
- Vendor A: cheaper per-token but no prefix caching / no token-level logs — emphasize observability
- Vendor B: strong latency but single-model stack — emphasize model catalog choice and verified profiles
- Vendor C: self-hosted runtime — emphasize no-ops hosted option + smooth upgrade to Dedicated/private

End.
